payload.source_label: Every constant real hyperbolic system decouples in an eigenbasis into scalar advection equations, with reconstruction of the state

contract.statement: For the homogeneous constant-coefficient system q_t + A q_x = 0 with real m-component states and a constant real m × m matrix A, the source defines hyperbolicity by real eigenvalues and a corresponding collection of m linearly independent eigenvectors. Every state vector then has a unique linear-combination representation in that selected eigenvector collection. The source announces that hyperbolic systems admit the scalar-wave decomposition illustrated by acoustics, with the corresponding eigenvalues serving as propagation speeds; the acoustic example has speeds −c and +c. The general transformation and its indexed PDE formula are not displayed in this paragraph, which points forward to Chapter 3. [Printed p. 1, (1.1) and following paragraph; printed p. 2, acoustic transformations after (1.6); printed p. 3, opening paragraph.]
assumptions: The governing equation is q_t + A q_x = 0 in the homogeneous, constant-coefficient, first-order linear setting. [Printed p. 1, (1.1) and surrounding paragraphs.]
For the asserted general wave decomposition, the system is hyperbolic: A has real eigenvalues and a corresponding set of m linearly independent eigenvectors. [Printed p. 3, opening paragraph.]
The selected passage is introductory prose containing a definition and explanatory claims, rather than a separately numbered theorem. [Printed p. 3, opening paragraph before (1.7).]

The general statement inherits the constant real matrix and one-dimensional homogeneous linear PDE setting from (1.1). [Printed p. 1, (1.1); printed p. 3, explicit reference to 'the constant-coefficient system (1.1)'.]
The acoustic example supplies the immediate meaning of decomposition into scalar wave equations. [Printed p. 2, equations for w^1 and w^2; printed p. 3, opening sentence.]

The reference to Chapter 3 announces later explanation; this paragraph does not identify a particular theorem or equation there as an additional hypothesis. [Printed p. 3, opening paragraph, 'As we will see in Chapter 3'.]
quantifiers: A system size m and state space R^m are inherited from equation (1.1); the passage specifies no explicit admissible range for m. [Printed p. 1, paragraph following (1.1).]
A is a constant real m × m matrix, and q : R × R → R^m depends on space x and time t. [Printed p. 1, (1.1) and following paragraph.]

There is a corresponding collection of m linearly independent eigenvectors with real eigenvalues; indexed notation r_i and λ_i, for i = 1,…,m, is an analyst naming convention for that collection. [Printed p. 3, opening paragraph, hyperbolicity criterion.]
The unique-decomposition claim quantifies over every vector v in R^m, relative to the selected collection of eigenvectors. [Printed p. 3, opening paragraph, 'any vector' and 'these eigenvectors'.]
